system: recombinant human MAP3K7 (O43318) expressed in baculovirus/insect cells
readout: ADP‑Glo luminescence (measure ADP produced by kinase activity)

steps.instruction: Prepare a 10‑point, 3‑fold serial dilution of CHEMBL1077979 in assay buffer with 0.5 % DMSO (vehicle) and include a no‑compound (0 % DMSO) and a known TAK1 inhibitor (e.g., 5 µM NG25) as reference controls.

parameters.top_concentration_uM: 30 µM (chosen to span >100‑fold above typical kinase IC50s reported for related MAP3K7 inhibitors)
parameters.vehicle_fraction: 0.5 % DMSO (v/v) – compatible with ADP‑Glo assay buffer

steps.instruction: In 384‑well plates combine recombinant MAP3K7 (final 5 nM), peptide substrate (e.g., MBP‑derived peptide at 10 µM), ATP (final 100 µM) and the diluted compound solutions; incubate 30 min at 30 °C.

parameters.enzyme_concentration: 5 nM (typical for linear range of ADP‑Glo with MAP3K7, see TAK1 assay examples)
parameters.substrate_concentration: 10 µM (saturating for MAP3K7, analogous to RB‑S6P used for TAK1)
parameters.ATP_concentration: 100 µM (near Km for ATP of MAP3K7, ensures competitive inhibition can be observed)
parameters.reaction_time: 30 min (short enough to stay in initial velocity, as used in TAK1 pre‑incubation assays)

steps.instruction: Add ADP‑Glo reagent to stop the reaction, deplete remaining ATP (10 min), then add detection reagent and incubate 30 min before reading luminescence on a plate reader.

parameters.reagent_volumes: 10 µL ADP‑Glo reagent per 20 µL reaction (per manufacturer protocol)

steps.instruction: Normalize luminescence to 0 % inhibition (no‑compound) and 100 % inhibition (reference inhibitor), fit a four‑parameter logistic curve, report IC50 with 95 % confidence interval and flag any curve‑fit warnings.

parameters.acceptance_criteria: R² > 0.90, Hill slope between 0.5 and 1.5, no systematic deviation of residuals

rationale: The retained examples show that MAP3K7 (TAK1 family) inhibition is routinely measured with peptide substrates and ADP‑Glo or radiometric readouts. A 5 nM enzyme and 100 µM ATP provide a robust signal‑to‑background while remaining within the linear range. A 30 µM top concentration ensures coverage of the expected potency range (sub‑nanomolar to low‑micromolar) without exceeding solubility limits for the moderately lipophilic CHEMBL1077979. Three‑fold dilutions give a smooth curve with sufficient data points. Replicates of three balance statistical power and plate‑throughput. Controls allow conversion of raw luminescence to percent inhibition and detection of assay drift.
citations: CHEMBL3823303 (AlphaScreen TAK1 assay – supports enzyme and substrate concentrations)
limitations: No direct biochemical IC50 for CHEMBL1077979 on MAP3K7 is available; potency estimate will be derived solely from this experiment.
Solubility of CHEMBL1077979 above 30 µM has not been confirmed; if precipitation occurs, the top concentration must be lowered (unresolved).
The assay uses a generic peptide substrate rather than a physiological MAP3K7 substrate; off‑target effects on substrate binding cannot be excluded.
Only a single enzyme construct (recombinant baculovirus‑expressed) is tested; post‑translational modifications present in cells may alter sensitivity (unresolved).
